templates.description: Irish traditional dance-music session palette: fiddle, tin whistle, uilleann pipes, wooden flute, bouzouki and bodhrán for reels, jigs, hornpipes and slow airs.
templates.treatment: Melody players share the tune in heterophony; rolls, cuts and crans on winds and pipes, bowed triplets on fiddle; bouzouki and bodhrán accompany.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Fiddle, whistle, wooden flute and uilleann pipes are long-standing; the Irish bouzouki entered the tradition in the late 1960s-70s.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Session pitch around D/G major and their modes (Dorian, Mixolydian) at A=440; uilleann pipes chanter in D (flat sets configurable).

templates.authenticity_note: A session-style palette for Irish dance tunes and airs. It does not represent any one regional style (e.g. Sliabh Luachra, Donegal, Clare) unless configured. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Scottish traditional palette with Great Highland bagpipe or bellows smallpipes, fiddle, clàrsach and frame drum for marches, strathspeys, reels and laments.
templates.treatment: Pipe drones throughout; grace-note gestures (doublings, throws) rather than tonguing; Scotch snap in strathspeys.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Great Highland bagpipe for outdoor and military contexts; smallpipes and Border pipes for indoor playing with fiddle; clàrsach revival instrument.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Highland pipe chanter sounds near Bb (written A) with its own just-leaning scale; smallpipes commonly in A or D. Choose one pipe track so tunings do not clash.

templates.authenticity_note: A Scottish traditional palette combining pipe, fiddle and harp idioms. Highland pipes and smallpipes rarely play together; the smallpipes track is optional. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Welsh folk palette centred on the triple harp with fiddle, voice and an optional historical crwth.
templates.treatment: Harp carries accompaniment patterns and variations (penillion style); crwth adds a bowed drone-heavy historical colour.

cultural_context.tradition: Welsh folk song, dance and harp tradition
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Triple harp (18th-19th c. onward); crwth is historical, with a modern reconstruction-based revival.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Diatonic/modal by default; crwth tuning follows period accounts and is a reconstruction (configurable).

templates.authenticity_note: A Welsh folk and harp palette. The crwth track is a historical reconstruction and should not be presented as a living mainstream sound. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: English folk and early-music palette: fiddle, lute, recorder and frame drum, with an optional 19th-century concertina for later folk settings.
templates.treatment: Pick an era first: medieval/Renaissance (lute, recorder, frame drum) or 19th-20th c. folk (fiddle, concertina).

cultural_context.tradition: English folk dance and song; medieval and Renaissance consort practice
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Lute, recorder and frame drum suit medieval/Renaissance settings; the concertina is a 19th-century invention.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Modal (Dorian, Mixolydian, Aeolian) by default; historical temperaments (Pythagorean, meantone) configurable.

templates.authenticity_note: A style-and-era-dependent English palette. Mixing the concertina with medieval instruments is anachronistic; it is optional and off by default for period work. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: German and Alpine folk palette with accordion, concert zither, brass ensemble, clarinet and double bass for Ländler, waltzes, polkas and marches.
templates.treatment: Oom-pah accompaniment in tuba/bass and brass after-beats; clarinet and accordion carry tunes; zither for intimate Stube textures.

cultural_context.subregion: Bavaria and the Alpine region (incl. Austria)
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Concert zither and diatonic Steirische accordion are Alpine; brass band (Blaskapelle) is widespread across German-speaking regions.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament, major keys dominant; yodel-like leaps in melodies.

templates.authenticity_note: A German and Alpine folk palette for dance and brass-band textures. It is not a model of commercial Volkstümliche Musik nor of any single regional Kapelle. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.display_name: Early Germanic / Medieval Central Europe — Speculative Reconstruction
templates.description: Speculative reconstruction palette with a Germanic round lyre, reconstructed frame drums, bone and wooden flutes and voice. Built from archaeological finds; no claim of exact original sound.
templates.treatment: Sparse, drone-based textures; lyre strums and plucked ostinati; chant-like voice; frame drum pulses.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Instruments modelled on archaeological finds (e.g. Trossingen and Sutton Hoo lyres, bone flutes); playing technique and repertoire are not documented.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Unknown. Default is a diatonic/pentatonic subset; lyre string count and tuning are assumptions and fully configurable.

templates.authenticity_note: Explicitly a speculative reconstruction. No claim is made about the exact original sound, tuning, repertoire or performance practice of early Germanic music, which is not documented. It is not a 'Viking' film sound either. Expert review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Scandinavian folk palette: Hardanger fiddle (Norway), nyckelharpa (Sweden), kantele (Finland) and an optional reconstructed tagelharpa.
templates.treatment: Drones and double-stops, sympathetic resonance, dense ornaments; asymmetric 3/4 polska feel with uneven beat lengths.

cultural_context.tradition: Scandinavian and Finnish folk fiddle and zither traditions
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Hardanger fiddle, nyckelharpa and kantele are living traditions; tagelharpa is a modern revival based on bowed-lyre evidence.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Hardanger scordaturas (e.g. AEAC#) and older non-tempered intonation are common; asymmetric polska timing is a performance choice, not encoded in the meter.

templates.authenticity_note: A pan-Nordic folk palette that groups national instruments for convenience. Each instrument belongs to a distinct national/regional tradition; choose the subset that fits the setting. Tagelharpa is reconstruction-based. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Andalusian flamenco palette: flamenco guitar, palmas, cajón (modern) and cante voice.
templates.treatment: Rasgueado and golpe on guitar, palmas sordas/claras on the compás, cajón as in post-1970s flamenco; Phrygian/Andalusian harmony.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Guitar and palmas are core; the cajón was adopted from Peru in the late 1970s and marks a modern flamenco sound.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Phrygian / 'modo flamenco' centre (e.g. E Phrygian with raised third); compás choice (soleá, bulería, tangos) sets the accent cycle.

templates.authenticity_note: A flamenco palette for Andalusian styles. Other Iberian folk traditions (Galician, Basque, Castilian) are distinct and not represented here. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: French folk and bal-musette palette: accordion, fiddle, hurdy-gurdy and flute for valses musette, bourrées and dance tunes.
templates.treatment: Hurdy-gurdy bourdons and trompette buzz for rural dances; accordion with musette (wet) tuning for the Parisian valse.

cultural_context.tradition: French traditional dance music and bal-musette
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Hurdy-gurdy is central to central-French dance tradition; accordion musette is an urban 20th-century Parisian style.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Accordion musette tuning (detuned reeds) and hurdy-gurdy drone pitches are configurable.

templates.authenticity_note: A palette mixing rural French dance and Parisian musette. These are distinct scenes; drop the hurdy-gurdy for a purely urban musette or the accordion for older rural settings. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Southern Italian folk palette with mandolin, accordion (organetto-style), tamburello and guitar for tarantella and pizzica.
templates.treatment: Tremolo picking on mandolin, driving tamburello in 6/8 or 12/8, guitar strums and accordion bass/chord.

cultural_context.tradition: Southern Italian tarantella and pizzica traditions
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Tamburello and organetto are central in the south; mandolin is strongly associated with Naples.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament, minor-major alternation common; vocal ornaments configurable.

templates.authenticity_note: A Southern Italian folk dance palette. Northern Italian traditions and the classical mandolin orchestra are different repertoires. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Balkan folk palette with clarinet, kaval, gaida, accordion and tapan, defaulting to Bulgarian/Macedonian dance meters.
templates.treatment: Asymmetric aksak meters (7/8, 9/8, 11/8); ornament-dense clarinet and kaval lines; tapan bass/switch strokes.

cultural_context.tradition: Bulgarian and Macedonian folk and wedding music
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Kaval, gaida and tapan are rural instruments; clarinet and accordion are central to 20th-century wedding bands.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament on clarinet/accordion; kaval and gaida have their own intonation; makam-influenced augmented seconds common.

templates.authenticity_note: A Bulgarian/Macedonian-leaning Balkan palette. Serbian, Greek, Romanian, Albanian and Romani brass traditions differ; choose and retag locally rather than treating 'Balkan' as one style. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Greek rebetiko and folk palette: bouzouki, baglamas, guitar and violin.
templates.treatment: Dromoi (modal paths) with taximi improvisations, tremolo and drone strings; zeibekiko 9/8 and hasapiko 2/4 feels.

cultural_context.tradition: Rebetiko and related Greek urban folk
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Three-course bouzouki and baglamas define classic rebetiko; four-course bouzouki is a later (1950s+) development.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Dromoi (e.g. Hijaz, Ousak, Rast) relate to makam/maqam; equal-tempered frets are the modern norm but microtonal inflection is configurable.

templates.authenticity_note: A rebetiko-centred Greek palette. Island (nisiotika) and mainland (dimotika) folk traditions use other instruments (lyra, laouto, clarinet). This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Turkish makam-oriented ensemble: oud, bağlama, ney, kanun and darbuka.
templates.treatment: Seyir (melodic path) within a makam; microtonal pitch bends and ornaments; usul rhythmic cycles on darbuka.

cultural_context.tradition: Turkish makam music (art and folk usage)
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Oud, ney and kanun belong to Ottoman/Turkish art music; bağlama is principally a folk (halk) instrument.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Makam pitch uses 53-comma (Arel-Ezgi-Uzdilek) theory; Western modes do not apply. Set a custom tuning table per makam.

templates.authenticity_note: A makam-oriented Turkish palette. It combines art-music and folk instruments for flexibility; it does not encode any specific makam or usul by default. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Selected Arab ensemble in the takht tradition: oud, qanun, ney, riq, darbuka and violin.
templates.treatment: Maqam-aware pitch bends with quarter-tone intervals; taqasim improvisation; iqa' rhythmic cycles on riq and darbuka.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Takht ensembles of oud, qanun, ney, violin and riq are associated with 19th-20th c. Egyptian and Levantine art music.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Maqam intervals including neutral seconds (quarter-tones); intonation varies by region. Western modes do not apply; use custom tuning.

templates.authenticity_note: A takht-style palette for maqam-based writing. Gulf, Iraqi maqam and Maghrebi traditions use different instruments and are separate presets. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Persian classical palette: tar, setar, santur, kamancheh, Persian ney and tombak for dastgah-based music.
templates.treatment: Melodic organization through dastgah and avaz with radif gushe-s; tahrir-like ornaments; tombak in free and metric sections.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: All instruments are standard in Persian classical ensembles.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Dastgah intervals include koron (lowered) and sori (raised) steps; not equal-tempered. Western modes do not apply; use custom tuning per dastgah.

templates.authenticity_note: A Persian classical palette for dastgah-aware writing. It does not encode any specific gushe, and Persian ney technique differs from the Turkish ney. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Hindustani palette: sitar or sarod, bansuri, tabla, tanpura drone and optional harmonium.
templates.treatment: Raga over a tanpura drone; alap-jor-jhala or bandish forms; meend and gamak; tala cycles (teental, jhaptal, rupak) on tabla.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Sitar, sarod, bansuri, tabla and tanpura are standard; harmonium is common in vocal and light-classical accompaniment.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Raga-specific just-leaning intonation relative to Sa; Western modes do not apply. Sa is configurable; set a custom tuning per raga.

templates.authenticity_note: A Hindustani palette for raga-and-tala writing. It does not define a raga; the tala meter shown is a notational convenience. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Carnatic palette: veena and/or violin, mridangam, ghatam, kanjira and tambura drone.
templates.treatment: Gamaka-rich raga phrasing; kriti and varnam forms; adi, rupaka and misra chapu talas; korvai and tani avartanam on percussion.

cultural_context.subregion: South India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana)
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Violin has been part of Carnatic practice since the 19th century, played seated with the scroll resting on the foot.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Raga-specific intonation with gamaka-defined svaras; Western modes do not apply. Set Sa and a custom tuning per raga.

templates.authenticity_note: A Carnatic palette for raga, tala and gamaka writing. Carnatic and Hindustani practices are distinct and are separate presets. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Chinese traditional chamber palette: erhu, pipa, guzheng, dizi, sheng and yangqin.
templates.treatment: Heterophonic ornamentation of a shared melody; slides, bends, tremolo plucks and glissandi; pentatonic modes (gong, shang, jue, zhi, yu).

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: All instruments are standard in Chinese ensembles; the modern guzheng (21 strings) and yangqin are 20th-century standardized forms.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Pentatonic modes mapped onto equal temperament by default; regional intonation (e.g. Chaozhou) configurable.

templates.authenticity_note: A Chinese traditional chamber palette. Regional styles (Jiangnan sizhu, Cantonese, Chaozhou, Northern guchui) differ; this is not a large modern Chinese orchestra. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Japanese traditional palette: koto, shakuhachi, shamisen and taiko, plus an optional festival shinobue.
templates.treatment: Breathy attacks and meri/kari bends on shakuhachi, bachi strikes and sawari on shamisen, koto bends; use of ma (space). Taiko only for festival or kumi-daiko contexts.

cultural_context.tradition: Hōgaku (sankyoku chamber music) and festival/kumi-daiko drumming
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Koto, shakuhachi and shamisen form sankyoku; kumi-daiko ensemble drumming is a post-1950s development distinct from chamber music.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Koto in hirajōshi or kumoijōshi by default; shakuhachi 1.8 shaku in D; equal temperament as an approximation.

templates.authenticity_note: A Japanese traditional palette spanning chamber music and taiko. Chamber (sankyoku), gagaku court music and taiko ensembles are distinct; taiko tracks are optional to keep them apart. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Korean traditional palette: gayageum, geomungo, daegeum, haegeum, optional piri and janggu.
templates.treatment: Nonghyeon vibrato and pitch-bending on strings and winds; jangdan rhythmic cycles (jinyangjo, jungmori, gutgeori) on janggu.

cultural_context.tradition: Gugak (Korean traditional music), incl. sanjo and court/folk ensembles
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: All instruments are standard in gugak; the 25-string gayageum is a modern extension.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Pentatonic modes (pyeongjo, gyemyeonjo) with expressive pitch bending; Western modes approximate only; custom tuning recommended.

templates.authenticity_note: A Korean gugak palette. Court music (jeongak) and folk/sanjo styles differ in tempo and ornament; it does not encode a specific jangdan. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Central Javanese gamelan palette: saron, gendèr, bonang, gong ageng, kempul, kenong, kendhang and suling.
templates.treatment: Colotomic cycles (gong, kempul, kenong punctuation) around a balungan melody; elaborating bonang and gendèr; kendhang leads irama changes.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Bronze instruments forged as a matched set; every gamelan has its own tuning.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Pélog (7-tone) or sléndro (5-tone) native tuning sets, unique per ensemble; not equal temperament. Use custom tuning tables.

templates.authenticity_note: A Javanese gamelan palette. Western MIDI pitches are placeholders for the ensemble's own pélog/sléndro tuning; Balinese gamelan is a separate preset. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Balinese gamelan palette (gong kebyar style): gangsa, reyong, gongs, kendang and ceng-ceng.
templates.treatment: Interlocking kotekan figuration between paired parts (polos/sangsih); sudden kebyar dynamic contrasts; ombak beating from paired tuning.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Gong kebyar is a 20th-century Balinese ensemble; instruments are tuned in pairs (pengumbang/pengisep).
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Local five-tone pélog-derived tuning with paired detuning (ombak); not equal temperament. Use custom tuning tables.

templates.authenticity_note: A Balinese gamelan palette. Distinct from Javanese gamelan; MIDI pitches are placeholders for the ensemble's tuning. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Thai piphat ensemble: ranat ek, khong wong yai, pi nai, taphon and ching.
templates.treatment: Heterophonic cyclic patterns around a core melody; ching marks metric cycles; ranat elaborates in octaves.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Standard piphat instruments; ensemble size varies (piphat khrueang ha, khrueang khu).
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Traditional Thai seven-tone near-equidistant tuning; Western equal temperament is an approximation. Use custom tuning.

templates.authenticity_note: A Thai piphat palette. Mahori and khrueang sai ensembles use strings and are not represented here. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Vietnamese traditional palette: đàn tranh, đàn bầu, đàn nguyệt, sáo trúc and optional đàn nhị.
templates.treatment: Heavy pitch bending and vibrato (rung, nhấn), harmonics on đàn bầu; regional modes (bắc, nam) shape ornament choice.

cultural_context.subregion: North, Central and South regional styles
cultural_context.tradition: Vietnamese traditional and chamber music (e.g. đờn ca tài tử)
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: All instruments are standard; đàn bầu is distinctively Vietnamese.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Pentatonic modal systems with regional pitch inflection (e.g. oán mode); equal temperament approximate; custom tuning recommended.

templates.authenticity_note: A Vietnamese traditional palette. Regional styles differ markedly; choose northern or southern ornament sets. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Mandé-inspired palette from the jali (griot) and drumming traditions: kora, balafon, djembe and dunun.
templates.treatment: Interlocking kora ostinati (kumbengo) with improvised runs (birimintingo); balafon patterns; djembe and dunun ensemble parts.

cultural_context.subregion: Mali, Guinea, Senegal, The Gambia (Mandé cultural area)
cultural_context.tradition: Mandé jali music and djembe/dunun drumming
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Kora and balafon are hereditary jali instruments; djembe and dunun ensemble drumming is related but socially distinct.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Kora tunings (silaba, tomora, hardino, sauta) and balafon tunings are maker-specific; configurable custom tuning.

templates.authenticity_note: A Mandé-inspired palette that combines jali instruments with djembe drumming. It identifies the Mandé lineage but does not represent a specific jali family's repertoire; drum parts are pattern templates, not specific rhythms. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Yoruba-related palette: dùndún talking drum, bàtá, bells, shekere and voice.
templates.treatment: Talking drum glides follow Yoruba speech tones; call and response with voice; bell timeline.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Dùndún ensembles are widespread; bàtá is associated with specific orisha (notably Ṣàngó) and some repertoire is ritual.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Talking-drum pitch follows the three-level tonal language; bells and drums are not tuned to Western scales.

templates.authenticity_note: A Yoruba-related drumming palette. Some bàtá and ritual repertoire is sacred; this preset supplies instruments and timeline templates only, not sacred rhythms, which should not be used without appropriate context. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Ewe drum ensemble from Ghana/Togo: gankogui bell, axatse rattle, and atsimevu, sogo, kidi and kagan drums.
templates.treatment: The bell timeline organizes cross-rhythms; support drums answer the master drum's signals; 12/8 with layered 3-against-2.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Standard Ewe ensemble instruments; specific pieces assign specific roles.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Drums are not pitch-tuned to scales; bell pitches vary by instrument.

templates.authenticity_note: An Ewe percussion palette built around the bell timeline. Ewe dances (Agbadza, Atsiagbekor, Gahu) differ in parts and meaning; patterns supplied are templates, not specific dance rhythms. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Central African palette with likembe lamellophone, drums and voices; intended to be specialized to a named community.
templates.treatment: Interlocking lamellophone patterns, layered drums and polyphonic voices; replace generic drum and vocal roles with community-specific metadata.

cultural_context.subregion: Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring countries
cultural_context.tradition: Selected Central African lamellophone and drum traditions
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Likembe is widespread in the region; drum and vocal roles are placeholders until a specific community tradition is curated.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Lamellophone tunings are maker- and community-specific; use custom tuning.

templates.authenticity_note: A deliberately general Central African starting point. Central Africa contains hundreds of distinct musical traditions; this is not a representation of any one of them, and community-specific metadata should be added before release. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Zimbabwean palette: mbira dzavadzimu (kushaura and kutsinhira parts), hosho, Zimbabwean marimba and vocals.
templates.treatment: Two interlocking mbira parts over a 48-pulse cycle; hosho triplet pulse; marimba ensemble as an optional modern layer; vocal huro/kushaura styles.

cultural_context.tradition: Shona mbira music; Zimbabwean marimba ensemble
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Mbira dzavadzimu has deep ceremonial roots (bira); the Zimbabwean marimba ensemble is a 1960s development.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Mbira tunings (e.g. nyamaropa, dambatsoko) vary by maker; use custom tuning, not equal temperament.

templates.authenticity_note: A Zimbabwean mbira-centred palette. Bira ceremonial contexts are spiritual; this palette supplies instruments and interlocking templates, not ceremonial repertoire. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.display_name: East Africa — Baganda & Luo Selected Traditions
templates.description: East African palette with the Baganda endongo lyre, amadinda xylophone and engoma drums, plus the Luo nyatiti lyre and vocals.
templates.treatment: Interlocking amadinda parts; lyre ostinati with sung lines; ensemble setup follows the chosen community.

cultural_context.tradition: Baganda court and folk music; Luo nyatiti tradition
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Endongo, amadinda and engoma are Baganda; nyatiti is Luo. They are grouped as options and should not be played together by default.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Baganda tuning is often described as near-equidistant pentatonic; nyatiti tunings are player-specific. Use custom tuning.

templates.authenticity_note: A grouped East African palette offering Baganda and Luo options. Baganda and Luo traditions are distinct communities; the nyatiti track is optional and the presets should be split once curated. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Maghrebi palette: oud, bendir, guembri and qraqeb (Gnawa), with optional ghaita and voices.
templates.treatment: Gnawa grooves (guembri ostinato, qraqeb triplet pulse) with call-and-response vocals; choose Gnawa, Andalusi or chaabi subgenre.

cultural_context.tradition: Maghrebi traditions incl. Gnawa, Andalusi and chaabi
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Guembri and qraqeb are Gnawa; oud belongs to Andalusi and chaabi; bendir is widespread.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Maghrebi modes (tubu') and Gnawa pentatonic usage; Western modes approximate only. Custom tuning available.

templates.authenticity_note: A Maghrebi palette with a Gnawa default. Gnawa lila ceremonies are spiritual; this preset supplies grooves and instruments, not ceremonial repertoire. Other subgenres need different instrument subsets. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Afro-Cuban dance ensemble: congas, bongos, timbales, claves, piano, bass, horns and optional tres.
templates.treatment: Everything aligns to the clave (2-3 or 3-2); piano montuno, bass tumbao, conga tumbao, bongo martillo, timbale cáscara and campana.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Tres and bongos come from son; timbales and horns from danzón/mambo big bands; salsa is a later New York-centred development.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament, Western harmony; clave direction is configurable.

templates.authenticity_note: An Afro-Cuban dance-ensemble palette. Sacred Afro-Cuban traditions (e.g. Lucumí bàtá) and rumba are separate repertoires not covered here. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Brazilian samba/choro palette: pandeiro, cavaquinho, seven-string guitar, surdo and tamborim, with optional flute.
templates.treatment: Sixteenth-note samba subdivision with swing-like lilt; cavaquinho centro rhythm; seven-string baixaria counterpoint (choro).

cultural_context.tradition: Samba de roda / samba carioca and choro
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Regional (choro) ensembles use flute, cavaquinho, guitars and pandeiro; surdo and tamborim belong to samba baterias.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament; Western functional harmony with chromatic passing chords.

templates.authenticity_note: A samba and choro palette. Choro (regional) and samba bateria are different ensembles; surdo/tamborim are optional for choro. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Tango palette: bandoneón, violin, piano, double bass and optional guitar.
templates.treatment: Marcato in 4 and síncopa accompaniments; arrastre drags into the beat; bandoneón bellows accents; chicharra and látigo effects on strings.

cultural_context.subregion: Buenos Aires / Montevideo (Río de la Plata)
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Bandoneón arrived from Germany in the late 19th century and became the voice of tango; guitar belongs to earlier and vocal tango.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament, minor-key harmony; Western functional harmony applies.

templates.authenticity_note: A tango palette (sexteto/orquesta típica core). Nuevo tango and electronic tango are separate stylistic choices. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Mariachi palette: violins, trumpets, vihuela, guitarrón and optional regional harp.
templates.treatment: Armonía of vihuela rasgueado and guitarrón bass; sesquiáltera (3/4 vs 6/8) in sones; trumpet and violin sections in thirds.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Modern mariachi format (violins, trumpets, vihuela, guitarrón) dates from the mid-20th century; harp is regional and older.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament; Western functional harmony.

templates.authenticity_note: A modern mariachi palette. Son jarocho, norteño and banda are separate Mexican traditions. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Andean ensemble palette: quena, siku/zampoña, charango, bombo and guitar.
templates.treatment: Siku ira/arka hocketing, quena ornaments, charango strumming and tremolo, bombo on head and rim; huayno and other forms.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Quena and siku are indigenous; charango and guitar are colonial-era string traditions; the mixed conjunto format grew in the 20th century.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Pentatonic and minor-mode material in equal temperament; siku sets can be tuned to other systems.

templates.authenticity_note: A mixed Andean conjunto palette. Community siku tropas and urban folk ensembles differ; this is not a specific community's practice. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Trinidad steelband palette: tenor, double-second, cello and bass pans plus engine-room percussion.
templates.treatment: Rolled sustained notes on pans, strummed chords on cello pans; engine room (iron, scratcher, drum kit, congas) drives calypso and soca.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Steel pans were developed in Trinidad from the 1930s-40s; engine-room percussion is integral to the steelband.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament on modern pans; layout per pan type.

templates.authenticity_note: A steelband palette. Other Caribbean traditions (reggae, mento, kompa) are separate. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Bluegrass string band: fiddle, five-string banjo, mandolin, acoustic guitar and upright bass.
templates.treatment: Three-finger banjo rolls, mandolin chop on the backbeat, flatpicked guitar runs, fiddle double-stops and slides; two-beat bass.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Bluegrass coalesced in the 1940s from old-time string band, blues and gospel; the banjo has West African roots.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament; major and mixolydian; fiddle tunings (cross-tuning) configurable.

templates.authenticity_note: A standard bluegrass band palette. Old-time string band music is related but distinct (clawhammer banjo, no chop). This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Reserved for community-approved instrument sets and metadata created in partnership with specific Indigenous nations. There is no universal default, and restricted or ceremonial material is protected and never shipped without consent.
templates.treatment: Opt-in, culturally specific sets only, each with community attribution and usage terms.

cultural_context.tradition: To be defined per partner nation
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: No instruments are provided until a specific community approves the instruments, names, metadata and usage terms.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Defined by each partner community.

templates.authenticity_note: This entry intentionally has no tracks. Indigenous musical traditions in North America are many and distinct, and some material is ceremonial or restricted. Content will only be added with community approval and attribution, and this entry cannot be instantiated until then. Review status: unreviewed; no sources yet.

templates.description: Film-score interpretation of Celtic colour: uilleann pipes or whistle solos over string orchestra, harp and frame-drum pulses. A cinematic approximation, not a traditional ensemble.
templates.treatment: Soaring solo airs with ornaments over legato strings; low drums and harp ostinati; choir pads optional.

cultural_context.region: Ireland / Scotland (as interpreted in film scoring)
cultural_context.tradition: Cinematic interpretation of Irish/Scottish traditional colour
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Traditional solo instruments placed in a Western orchestral context; this blend is a screen convention.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament; uilleann pipes in D; modal (Dorian/Mixolydian/Aeolian) harmony.

templates.authenticity_note: A cinematic interpretation of Celtic colour for film and games. It is not traditional Irish or Scottish music; use the 'Ireland — Traditional Session' or 'Scotland' presets for that. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Film-score hybrid drawing on Chinese and Japanese solo instruments over strings, taiko and synth pads. A cinematic approximation that mixes traditions, not a traditional ensemble.
templates.treatment: Solo erhu or shakuhachi lines; koto/guzheng ostinati; taiko hits and processed percussion; string beds.

cultural_context.region: East Asia (as interpreted in film scoring)
cultural_context.tradition: Cinematic hybrid of East Asian instrumental colour
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Mixes Chinese and Japanese instruments that do not normally play together; chosen for screen colour.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament; pentatonic and phrygian-leaning harmony.

templates.authenticity_note: A cinematic hybrid for film and games. It deliberately mixes national traditions and is not representative of Chinese or Japanese music; consider using a single tradition's preset when the story is set in a specific place. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.display_name: Middle East & North Africa — Cinematic Interpretation
templates.description: Film-score interpretation using oud, ney, qanun and frame drums over strings, low percussion and a solo voice. A cinematic approximation, not a maqam ensemble.
templates.treatment: Phrygian-dominant and double-harmonic colour in equal temperament; ornamented solo lines; driving darbuka and low drums.

cultural_context.region: Middle East / North Africa (as interpreted in film scoring)
cultural_context.tradition: Cinematic interpretation of Arab, Turkish and Maghrebi colour
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Instruments from several distinct traditions combined for screen colour; Western scales replace maqam by default.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament with phrygian_dominant / double_harmonic approximations; maqam tuning optional.

templates.authenticity_note: A cinematic interpretation for film and games. Equal-tempered 'exotic' scales are not maqam; use the Arab, Türkiye, Iran or Maghrebi presets for tradition-specific writing, and avoid generic 'desert' stereotyping. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Film-score interpretation with quena and siku over strings, charango, harp and soft percussion. A cinematic approximation, not a traditional conjunto.
templates.treatment: Breathy quena solos and siku hockets over sustained strings; charango tremolo shimmer; restrained bombo.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Andean winds and charango in a Western orchestral context.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament; minor and pentatonic harmony.

templates.authenticity_note: A cinematic interpretation for film and documentary. It is not traditional Andean music; use 'Andes — Selected Ensemble' for that. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Film-score interpretation with tagelharpa and Hardanger fiddle drones, low male voices, frame drums and low strings. A cinematic approximation; no historical claim.
templates.treatment: Drone-based harmony, throat-voice and chant pads, frame-drum pulses and low-string swells.

cultural_context.tradition: Cinematic interpretation of Nordic folk and reconstruction colour
cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Mixes living Nordic folk instruments with reconstruction-based ones (tagelharpa) for screen colour.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament; Aeolian/Dorian drones.

templates.authenticity_note: A cinematic 'saga' interpretation for film and games. It makes no claim about Viking-age music, which is largely undocumented; see the 'Early Germanic' reconstruction and 'Nordic — Scandinavian Folk' presets. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.

templates.description: Contemporary fusion palette pairing sitar, bansuri and tabla with drum kit, bass, synth pads and strings. A fusion interpretation, not Hindustani classical practice.
templates.treatment: Raga-flavoured melodies over Western harmony and grooves; tabla layered with kit; drone pads replace tanpura.

cultural_context.instrument_provenance: Hindustani instruments in a Western pop/electronic and orchestral context.
cultural_context.tuning_assumptions: Equal temperament by default; raga-derived scales approximated; custom tuning optional.

templates.authenticity_note: A contemporary fusion palette. Equal-tempered raga approximations are not raga practice; use 'India — Hindustani' or 'India — Carnatic' for classical work. This is a starting palette, not a claim of authenticity; expert and community review is pending. Tuning, temperament, scale and ornament set are configurable per track; nothing here is fixed by the template.
